description: Defines the biological context before a perturbation is applied (cell model, genotype, disease state, prior treatments). This establishes background conditions but is not a causal claim to be falsified.
Represents a direct physical binding event between two biomolecules (e.g., drug-target, protein-protein, ligand-receptor). Binding strength should be specified via affinity (nM) when known.
signature: binds_to(id, actor, target, {affinity, unit, residues_actor, residues_target, via, confidence})

description: Causal modulation of the functional activity of a single molecule (protein, enzyme, transporter, transcription factor, or RNA). Requires explicit direction = up (increase activity) or down (decrease activity).
Causal modulation of the activity of a defined pathway or process (e.g., MAPK signaling, autophagy, EMT). Requires explicit direction = up or down.
Causal effect on the assembly, disassembly, or stoichiometry of a molecular complex. Requires explicit direction = up (promotes assembly/stabilization) or down (causes disassembly/destabilization).
signature: modulates_complex(id, members, complex, direction, {stoichiometry, via, confidence})

description: Alters the steady-state RNA levels or isoform ratios of one or more genes. Requires explicit direction = up (increased expression) or down (decreased expression). Optional mechanism tags (e.g., alternative splicing).
signature: regulates_expression(id, regulator, gene_list, direction, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Causal modulation of protein synthesis at the ribosome level (e.g., eIF inhibition, uORF/IRES usage). Requires explicit direction = up (increased translation) or down (decreased translation).
signature: regulates_translation(id, regulator, rna_id, direction, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Addition or removal of a post-translational modification (e.g., phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation) or cleavage at a specific site. Requires explicit direction = up (addition/increase) or down (removal/decrease).
signature: post_translational_modification(id, protein, mod_type, site, direction, {via, confidence})

description: Causal movement of an entity between compartments (e.g., cytoplasm → nucleus, secretion, uptake). Must specify both source and destination. Optional mechanism field for transport process (e.g., exocytosis).
signature: localises_to(id, entity, from_loc, to_loc, {mechanism, via, confidence})

description: Enzymatic conversion of one substrate into another product.

Causal modulation of target protein stability/abundance via half-life changes (e.g., ubiquitin-proteasome degradation, PROTAC-induced degradation, chaperone stabilization). Requires explicit direction = up (stabilization/increased abundance) or down (degradation/reduced abundance).
A genetic alteration (variant, mutation, or edit) that increases the functional activity of a protein relative to wild type.
A genetic alteration (variant, mutation, knockdown, knockout) that decreases or abolishes the activity of a protein relative to wild type.
Causal induction or worsening of a measurable phenotype or cell-state transition (e.g., proliferation, EMT, senescence). Optional `from_state`/`to_state` capture state transitions.
signature: induces_phenotype(id, source, phenotype, {via, confidence, from_state, to_state})

description: Causal mitigation or rescue of a phenotype, shifting it toward normal. Optional `from_state`/`to_state` capture state transitions.
signature: alleviates_phenotype(id, actor, phenotype, {via, confidence, from_state, to_state})

description: Non-causal functional similarity between two entities (transcriptomic, phenotypic, structural). Does not imply mechanistic regulation.
Statistical association between two entities without implying causality (e.g., GWAS hits, co-expression).
Background annotation linking an entity to a pathway, GO term, or cellular compartment.
Causal ligand-receptor signaling between two cell types, including the immediate downstream outcome. Outcome direction must be specified when modulation is implied (up/down).
signature: cell_cell_interaction(id, sender, receiver, ligand, receptor, outcome, {via, confidence})

description: Addition or removal of a histone/DNA mark at a genomic locus, altering chromatin accessibility. Requires explicit direction = up (addition/increased marking) or down (removal/decreased marking).
